{{small|(Managing Director & CEO)}}|Narinder Kumar Jain
{{small|(Managing Director)}}{{cite web|title=Key People Of Cosco India|url=http://www.securities.com/Public/company-profile/IN/Cosco_India_Ltd_en_1622177.html|publisher=securities.com|access-date=23 August 2013}}}} | area_served = | industry = [[Sports equipment]], [[fitness equipment]] | products = | operating_income = 125.79 crore (March 2016){{cite web|title=Net Operating Income of COSCO India|url=http://www.moneycontrol.com/financials/coscoindia/results/quarterly-results/CI18|publisher=moneycontrol.com|access-date=23 August 2013 |last1=Com |first1=Moneycontrol }} | assets = 40.67 crore (March 2012) | num_employees = 1001–2500{{cite web|title=Cosco India No of Employees|url=https://jcustomercare.com/cosco-india-new-delhi-address-phone-number-website-details/|access-date=10 October 2014}} | website = [http://www.cosco.in/ www.cosco.in] | footnotes = }} '''Cosco (India) Ltd.''' is an Indian [[sports equipment]] manufacturer based in [[Delhi]].{{cite web|title=Cosco Products|url=http://cosco.in/india.htm|publisher=cosco limited|access-date=23 August 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130828043605/http://cosco.in/india.htm|archive-date=28 August 2013|url-status=dead}} Cosco makes equipment for multiple sports, among them [[basketball]], [[association football|football]], [[volleyball]], [[handball]], [[cricket]], [[tennis]], [[Rackets (sport)|rackets]], [[table tennis]], and [[roller skating]] as well as [[Exercise equipment|fitness equipment]]. ==History== The company was founded on 25 January 1980 under the [[Companies Act, 1956]]. Cosco was a sister company of Enkay India Rubber Company, Pvt. Ltd., which also produces sports equipment. Cosco was a private company until 15 March 1994 after which it went [[Public company|public]]. After its [[Incorporation (business)|incorporation]], it took over the partnership Firm Coronation Sportingball Co., founded in 1976, a producer of [[Ball|sports balls]]. The company's shares are traded on India's [[BSE SENSEX]]. The company is part of the World Federation of the Sporting Goods Industry, the Sports Goods Export Promotion Council and the Sports Goods Foundation of India. ==Sponsorship== Most tournaments in India use Cosco products.{{cite web|title=Cosco Recognition 1|url=http://cosco.in/awards.htm|publisher=cosco|access-date=23 August 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130807060900/http://cosco.in/awards.htm|archive-date=7 August 2013|url-status=dead}} Cosco was the official sports partner for 2015's [[2015 National Games of India|35th National Games]] in [[Kerala]] for football, table tennis and handball.http://www.kerala2015.com/news/cosco-nivia-be-official-sport-partners.Cosco{{Dead link|date=November 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Platina Foot Ball "The Official Ball" of 128th Edition of [[Durand Cup]], 2016 and 57th Edition of [[Subroto Cup]] Foot Ball Tournament, 2016{{Dead link|date=July 2025}} ===Football=== ====State level teams==== * {{flagicon|Kerala}} [[Kerala football team|Kerala]] ====Clubs==== * {{flagicon|BAN}} [[Sheikh Russel KC|Sheikh Russel]] (2018−2024) * {{flagicon|BAN}} [[Mohammedan Sporting Club (Dhaka)|Mohammedan Sporting Club]] (2018−2021) * {{flagicon|BHU}} [[Thimphu F.C.|Thimphu]] (2018−) * {{flagicon|BHU}} [[Druk Star F.C.|Druk Star]] (2018−) * {{flagicon|BHU}} [[Druk United F.C.|Druk United]] (2018−) * {{flagicon|BHU}} [[Ugyen Academy F.C.|Ugyen Academy]] (2018−) * {{flagicon|IND}} [[Bhawanipore FC]] (2018−) * {{flagicon|IND}} [[Hindustan F.C.|Hindustan]] (2014−) * {{flagicon|IND}} [[Kenkre F.C.|Kenkre]] (2016−17) * {{flagicon|IND}} [[F.C. extract:
Cosco (India) Ltd. is an Indian sports equipment manufacturer based in Delhi.
Cosco makes equipment for multiple sports, among them basketball, football, volleyball, handball, cricket, tennis, rackets, table tennis, and roller skating as well as fitness equipment.
